messages:
lucy: Trying to get a sample app running with `redwoodctl localserve` after onboarding. I followed the quickstart, created a second profile 'staging' in ~/.redwood/config, and now localserve keeps picking the wrong profile (uses default) despite REDWOOD_PROFILE=staging. Anyone seen env var being ignored?

hannah: Is the env var exported in the same shell where you run localserve? Also check for a profile override in the localserve config file `.redwood/local.yaml` in the repo. We recently added an explicit per-app override and it can shadow REDWOOD_PROFILE.

lucy: Ah, there's a `.redwood/local.yaml` in the project that has `profile: default`. I didn't notice that in the quickstart. Maybe the sample scaffold should call this out.

mero: Good catch. Quick explanation: precedence is CLI flag > .redwood/local.yaml > REDWOOD_PROFILE env var > global config default. That ordering was intentional for reproducible dev environments, but onboarding fails to surface it.

lucy: I only saw REDWOOD_PROFILE mentioned in the docs. The scaffold should either not write a default profile or should prefer env var for first-time users.

hannah: Agree. Proposal: change quickstart scaffold to omit `profile:` in `.redwood/local.yaml` and add a short note in the onboarding CLI output: "We detected REDWOOD_PROFILE set — to use it, ensure your project config does not pin `profile:`." Also add `--profile` to `localserve` help text.

mero: We'll also add a diagnostic message when localserve starts saying which config source decided the profile, something like: "Using profile 'default' (source: .redwood/local.yaml). To override set REDWOOD_PROFILE or use --profile." That should reduce confusion.

lucy: That would have saved me time. For now I removed the `profile:` line and localserve picked staging. Confirmed.

devex-bot: Filed DX-5012: "onboard: scaffold .redwood/local.yaml without profile, surface config precedence in localserve startup message, add --profile help text". Assigned to @hannah and @mero.
